title: Learn why quotes get turned down, one short answer at a time
one_liner: When you mark an estimate as lost, you get a one-tap prompt for the reason, and each month the answers are sorted into plain patterns you can act on.
steps: In your CRM or estimate tool, mark a quote 'lost' when the customer says no or goes silent for good.
Your automation tool texts or emails the owner or salesperson: 'Why did [customer first name] pass? Pick one or add a line.'
The reply (price, timing, went with someone else, project cancelled, other) is logged in a Google Sheet next to the quote value and job type.
On the first of the month, an AI step groups the reasons and free-text notes into themes and counts them.
You read the one-page summary and decide what, if anything, to change about pricing, response time or scope.
guardrail: The AI only groups what your team typed in; a person decides whether a pattern means changing prices, follow-up or the offer.
tools: Your CRM or estimating tool (HubSpot, Jobber, Housecall Pro, Pipedrive), Zapier, Make or n8n, Google Sheets, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), SMS or Gmail
prompt:
You summarize why a small local business lost quotes last month. Use only the rows below. Do not invent reasons, counts or customer details, and do not name customers.

Business: [business name]
Month: [month and year]
Rows (job type | quote amount | reason picked | free-text note):
[paste rows from the sheet]

Return:
1. Count of lost quotes and total quote value lost (add up the amounts shown; if an amount is blank, say how many were blank).
2. Reasons ranked by count, each with the number of quotes and a short quoted phrase from the notes if one exists.
3. Any pattern by job type (only if at least 3 rows support it; otherwise say 'not enough rows').
4. Two questions the owner could ask the team, phrased as questions, not recommendations.
If there are fewer than 5 rows, say 'too few rows for patterns' and just list them.
source_name: Zapier win-loss / closed-lost reason templates (search results)
verification_note: Fixed output, no-names rule, counts only from rows, and a minimum-rows exit; a model would return a short compliant summary without inventing causes.

title: Spot tomorrow's staffing gap tonight and get a fix drafted for you to approve
one_liner: Each evening your schedule is checked against what tomorrow's bookings need, and if you're short, you get a plain list of the gap plus a drafted message to your backup people.
steps: Keep a simple sheet of tomorrow's jobs or appointments and who is scheduled, plus a list of backup people and their usual availability.
At 5 pm an automation reads the sheet and counts people needed versus people scheduled for each time block.
If a block is short, an AI step drafts a short message to the backup list asking who can cover, with the date, hours and place filled in.
The manager gets an email or text with the gap and the draft, and taps approve or edits it.
Only after approval does the message go out; replies are logged back in the sheet.
guardrail: Nothing is sent to staff until the manager approves it, and the manager chooses who actually covers.
tools: Google Sheets or your scheduling app, n8n, Make or Zapier, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Gmail or SMS (Twilio)
prompt:
You help a small local business manager fill a staffing gap for tomorrow. Use only the details below. Do not promise pay, overtime or perks that are not listed, and do not choose a person; just write the ask.

Business: [business name]
Date: [date]
Short block(s): [time block | role needed | people scheduled | people needed]
Location: [address or site name]
What the shift involves: [one sentence]
Pay or terms to mention (only if provided): [terms or 'none']
Manager name: [name]

Write:
1. A two-line summary for the manager: what is short and by how many.
2. A text message under 320 characters to the backup list asking who can cover, ending with 'Reply YES with your name by [deadline].'
Tone: friendly, plain, no pressure. If the sheet data looks inconsistent (for example needed is less than scheduled), say 'Check the sheet' and write nothing else.
source_name: n8n 'plan and approve standby staffing recovery' template (search results)
verification_note: Prompt restricts to supplied facts, caps the SMS length, bars invented pay and has an inconsistent-data exit; a model would produce a short summary and a compliant ask.

title: See which days, times and services your no-shows cluster on
one_liner: Every Monday you get a short readout of last week's no-shows and cancellations grouped by service and time slot, so you can adjust reminders or booking rules with evidence.
steps: Whenever an appointment is marked no-show or late-cancelled, log service, day, start time and lead time to a Google Sheet.
Every Monday morning the automation pulls the last four weeks of rows alongside total bookings for the same period.
An AI step writes the rates by service and by time block and flags only differences backed by enough rows.
The summary is emailed to the owner or front-desk lead.
They decide whether to change reminder timing, require deposits for a slot, or leave things alone.
guardrail: The AI reports counts and rates only; a person decides any booking, deposit or reminder rule change, and no customer is flagged or blocked automatically.
tools: Your booking tool (Acuity, Square Appointments, Jobber, Calendly), Zapier, Make or n8n, Google Sheets, an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Gmail
prompt:
You analyze appointment no-shows for a small local business. Use only the numbers below. Do not invent causes, and do not name or describe individual customers.

Business: [business name]
Period: [start date] to [end date]
Totals by service (service | bookings | no-shows | late cancels):
[paste]
Totals by day and time block (day | block | bookings | no-shows | late cancels):
[paste]

Return:
1. Overall no-show rate (no-shows divided by bookings) and late-cancel rate, rounded to whole percent.
2. The top 2 services and top 2 time blocks by no-show rate, but only where bookings are at least 8; otherwise say 'not enough bookings'.
3. One sentence per finding saying what the numbers show, not why it happens.
4. Two options the owner could test (for example an earlier reminder or a deposit for one slot), labeled as options.
If total bookings are under 30, say 'too few bookings for patterns' and give only item 1.
source_name: n8n no-show reminder and weekly report templates (search results)
verification_note: Minimum-bookings thresholds and a no-causes rule keep output factual; a model would return rates and two testable options without fabricated reasons.

title: Tell your team when a customer praises them by name
one_liner: When a new review names someone on your team, a short kudos note is drafted for you to approve and share, so good work gets noticed the same week.
steps: Your automation tool watches for new Google reviews of 4 stars or more.
An AI step checks the text against your staff list (first names and nicknames) and extracts the matching name and the exact praise.
If there is a match, it drafts a two-sentence kudos message quoting the praise.
The owner or manager gets the draft by email or Slack and approves, edits or skips it.
Approved notes are posted to the team channel and logged in a sheet for review time.
guardrail: A person approves every kudos message, and anything ambiguous (a name shared by two staff, or a mixed review) is skipped, not guessed.
tools: Google Business Profile review trigger via Zapier, Make or n8n, Google Sheets (staff list), an AI model (Claude or ChatGPT), Slack or Gmail
prompt:
You help a small local business recognize staff who are named in customer reviews. Use only the review text and staff list below. Do not guess who a customer meant.

Business: [business name]
Staff list (first name | nickname | role): [list]
Review stars: [number]
Review text: [paste review]

If the review names exactly one person on the staff list, return:
Staff member: [name]
Quoted praise: [short exact quote from the review]
Kudos draft: [two sentences, warm and plain, from [manager name], quoting the praise]
If the review names nobody, names someone not on the list, matches more than one staff member, or complains about anything, return only: 'Skip - needs a person to read.' Do not include the reviewer's full name or any contact details.
source_name: Zapier Google Business Profile review-to-Slack templates (search results)
verification_note: Strict single-match rule with a skip exit and exact-quote requirement; a model would either produce a clean kudos or the skip line.
